subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should the incremental session-memory fix be implemented fresh against current main, rescued from the conflicting candidate PR, or intentionally rejected in favor of full-entry consistency plus cache/delta controls?
rationale: The choice affects persistent memory-index behavior, session-state correctness, chunk overlap, compaction fallback, source-wide batching, and whether the existing contributor branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory-core schema and batching paths with real behavior proof.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete schema assumptions before review continues.

options.title: Reject incremental indexing
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide full-entry consistency plus existing embedding cache and delta thresholds are preferable to incremental complexity.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement incremental preservation against the current memory-core schema and batching paths with real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-memory and batching history makes this the best available owner for the schema and batching design choice.
